newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa to launch yen issue in June - paper.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa to launch yen issue in June - paper.

text.p: South Africa had decided on a yen issue in June to kick off its four billion rand foreign borrowing programme, Business Day newspaper said on Thursday.
Quoting finance director-general Maria Ramos it said the finance department was interviewing banks to pick a lead manager for a Samurai bond issue in Tokyo.
Ramos also told the paper that South Africa was planning another dollar issue later in the year, after last year's Yankee bond.
Ramos declined to disclose the amount to be raised by the yen issue, but market speculation was that it would be larger than the last Samurai issue 30 billion yen, the paper said.
This would comprise the lion's share of overall foreign borrowing this fiscal year, seen as a sensible move as the rand has strengthened considerably against the yen.
Business Day said government was looking at a maturity on the issue of about seven years.
A roadshow was planned for Japan in June, after a bank had been picked to manage the issue.
South Africa's last Samurai issue, in 1995, was lead managed by Daiwa but Ramos could not confirm that it was a contender, the paper said.
